object_description: compact five-story solitary building with a notched intermediate level
design_condition: The solitary building is placed within the park-like site with a small footprint, creating broad open-space edges and windmill-like outdoor areas, but its dense edges and paths weaken arrival, permeability, and existing landscape structure.

positive.statement: The compact building creates a harmonious relationship between built mass and surrounding open space.
The small footprint provides sufficiently wide edges for outdoor spaces.
The outdoor spaces offer a rich range of uses for the surrounding area.
The communal level is surrounded by an attractive exterior space that invites people to linger.
The hybrid timber structure is plausibly designed and reduces the concrete-intensive base to lower levels.
The rigorous urban-planning approach achieves the smallest possible footprint.

negative.statement: The dense arrangement of pitches and parking lacks clear addressing and an appropriate spacious arrival situation.
A pitch at the corner blocks an important diagonal path and endangers existing trees.
The doubled path system is incomprehensible and conflicts with the existing meandering routes.
The communal outdoor area is too small for a kindergarten and cannot replace an outdoor play garden.
Classrooms without views to the outside cannot be accepted for permanent work areas.
The floor plans do not allow the required clustering of classrooms and group rooms.
The structural solution for the overhang of the upper floors is unclear.
The building’s scale, escape balconies and informal escape stair give it a commercial-looking character.
